passage: At lunch in the Pune school canteen, Ishita watched Pranav walk up to the group's table with his tray. Riya turned her shoulder. Nimisha slid her bag onto the empty chair without a word. When Pranav asked, "Can I sit?" nobody answered, as if he had said it to the wall. Ishita stared at her rice, her ears warm. She wanted to say something, but the words sat like stones. Pranav stood for another second, then took his tray to the window ledge. All afternoon her stomach felt heavy. Next day in chemistry, she asked him quietly, "Want to be lab partners? I haven't picked yet." Pranav looked surprised. "Okay." It was a very small thing, and she was still shaking a little when she wrote her name on the sheet.

qa.q: Where did Pranav take his tray after nobody answered him?
qa.a: He took it to the window ledge.

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling while the group ignored Pranav?
qa.a: She felt ashamed and stuck. Her ears went warm and she wanted to speak, but the words sat like stones.

qa.q: What small step did Ishita take, and why was it a good choice?
qa.a: She asked Pranav to be her lab partner. It was a quiet way to include him without needing to confront the whole group.

qa.q: How might Pranav have felt when Ishita asked him?
qa.a: Surprised, and maybe relieved to be noticed. He said "Okay" after looking surprised, after being ignored the day before.

grounding: Ishita stays silent while her group freezes someone out, feels guilty, and quietly befriends the excluded boy the next day.

passage:
"Guys, why is Kalyani coming over here?"
"Don't look at her. Just keep talking."
"Hi… can I sit?"
Silence. Tara stared at her phone. Anand stared at his samosa. His face was hot.
"Oh, sorry, these seats are taken," someone said. They were not taken.
Kalyani stood there a second too long, then walked away.
"Good," said Tara. "She's so clingy."
Anand's chest felt tight. He had known Kalyani since Class 4. She had shared her geography map with him last week.
"She's not clingy," he said quietly. "She's just new to this section."
"Anand, whose side are you on?"
He didn't answer. After the bell, he caught up with Kalyani near the lockers. "Hey. That was rubbish of us. Of me. Want to sit with me at lunch tomorrow? Just us, on the steps."
Kalyani looked at him for a long moment. "Okay," she said. "The steps."

qa.q: What did Kalyani share with Anand last week?
How did Anand feel as the group froze Kalyani out?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and tense, his face hot and chest tight as he stayed silent while she was turned away.

qa.q: What small steps did Anand take to make things right?
qa.a: He spoke up briefly for Kalyani to the group, then apologised to her and invited her to eat with him on the steps.

qa.q: How might Kalyani see Anand's apology?
qa.a: She seems cautious but open, looking at him for a long moment before accepting because he had stayed silent earlier.

grounding: A teen who silently watches his group freeze out a classmate feels ashamed, speaks up a little and quietly befriends her.

passage:
For most of Class 10, the girls in my group froze Salma out. It started over something tiny, a birthday invitation, and grew into months of silence: nobody passing her the notebook, nobody saving her a seat on the bus.
I was Jeevan, the one who stayed quiet. I told myself it wasn't my fight. The truth is I was scared that if I said anything, I'd be next.
Every time I saw Salma eating alone, I felt ashamed. I'd go home and feel sick about it.
In physics lab, we got paired by roll number. I could have kept quiet there too. Instead I pushed the beaker over and said, "You do the readings, I'll write?" She looked surprised. By the end of the term we did every lab together.
It wasn't brave. It was small. But it was better than joining in, which I'd almost done more than once.

qa.q: Where did Jeevan and Salma get paired?
qa.a: In physics lab, by roll number.

qa.q: Why did Jeevan feel unable to speak up for so long?
qa.a: Jeevan felt afraid of being the next person frozen out, and felt ashamed every time Salma ate alone.

qa.q: What small step did Jeevan take, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Jeevan started working with Salma in physics lab, a quiet act of friendship that went against the group's exclusion.

qa.q: What was Class 10 like for Salma?
qa.a: Salma likely felt lonely and rejected, eating alone and having no one pass her a notebook or save her a seat.

grounding: A teen who silently watched a group freeze someone out feels ashamed and quietly befriends the excluded classmate.
